text: The 1992 European Tour, known as the 1992 Volvo Tour due to sponsorship, marked the 21st season of the main professional golf tour in Europe, which began in 1972. It was the fifth season under a title sponsorship agreement with Volvo, announced in May 1987. The tour made its first foray into East Asia by including the Johnnie Walker Asian Classic in Thailand in its schedule. The season consisted of 38 tournaments that counted toward the Order of Merit and five non-counting "Approved Special Events." Changes from the prior season included the return of the Dubai Desert Classic, the Tenerife Open, and the Moroccan Open; the addition of the Johnnie Walker Asian Classic, the Turespaña Masters Open de Andalucía, the Roma Masters, the Lyon Open V33, and the Honda Open; and the removal of the Girona Open, the Murphy's Cup, the European Pro-Celebrity, and the Epson Grand Prix of Europe. A table listed the official events of the 1992 season. Several events were sanctioned by the European Tour but did not award official money or count as wins. The Order of Merit was officially named the Volvo Order of Merit and was determined by the total prize money earned during the season, calculated in Pound sterling.
